entries.symptom: Required CI interpretation could become unsafe or unavailable when check identity, legacy commit-status evidence, or policy access was incomplete.
entries.root_cause: The first resolver modeled check names but not every authority dimension needed for fail-closed promotion.
entries.fix: Require explicit mergeable check states, retain app identity, ingest Commit Status evidence, and classify inaccessible live policy as UNCERTAIN.
entries.verification: Exact-head preflight and fresh PR CI passed after regression coverage for unrecognized states, wrong-app checks, legacy statuses, and inaccessible policy.
entries.regression_protection: Dedicated decision, GitHub-evidence, and required-check resolver tests exercise each repaired failure mode.
entries.residual_risk: Required-workflow rules remain UNCERTAIN until mapped to concrete workflow evidence; this is an intentional fail-closed limitation.

entries.symptom: Pre-change risk predictor marked an unrelated Everward subsystem as HISTORICAL_SIGNALS_PRESENT.
entries.root_cause: Area-learning similarity included generic repository/path tokens such as src and simulation, so weak structural overlap was mistaken for meaningful domain overlap.
entries.fix: Filter generic path/repository tokens from risk matching and require either an explicit path match or at least one informative matched token before a lesson contributes to the risk profile.
entries.verification: Exact-head full preflight passed on commit 9675dab700fada6b6fa5c6a02f45b1261dbf7cc4 with 269 tests passing, including a regression test for unrelated same-repository paths.
entries.regression_protection: Pre-change risk matching must ignore generic structural tokens and preserve NO_RELEVANT_VERIFIED_HISTORY when no informative area match exists.
entries.residual_risk: New generic tokens introduced by future repository layouts may require extending the bounded generic-token set; explicit path matches remain authoritative evidence.

entries.symptom: Research Report conclusion rows could classify evidence as class-level, indirect-context, or unavailable without explicitly naming the missing direct evidence, allowing a structurally valid report to obscure an important evidence gap.
entries.root_cause: The report parser validated evidence IDs and directness values independently but did not couple non-direct classifications to the required missing_direct_evidence disclosure.
entries.fix: Mirror the model-facing evidence-boundary instruction with a deterministic parser invariant that rejects class-level, indirect-context, or unavailable rows when missing_direct_evidence is null, and add regression coverage for the hidden-gap case.
entries.verification: Exact implementation head 7aae594b26b9834300702ad6798086c680329b99 passed canonical preflight before PR creation and fresh PR CI for Quality, Golden Verification, Security, Control Plane, and Execution Director before merge in knowledge-engine-ai#162.
entries.regression_protection: Research Report parser tests must fail closed when non-direct evidence classifications omit explicit missing-direct-evidence disclosure; prompt guidance remains additive rather than authoritative.
entries.residual_risk: Structural directness validation does not prove that free-text report citations resolve to known EvidenceRecord IDs or that the final report is semantically correct and readable; those require separate deterministic citation checks and Product Reality acceptance.

entries.symptom: Two wrong diagnoses were reported to the owner and ChatGPT during the 2026-11-11 engine stall: that three knowledge-engine repositories had no capability graph, and that one stuck draft suppressed all local planning.
entries.root_cause: Both claims were built from unfiltered listings of flow-state/iron-god-products/roadmap-requests/, which keeps stale request files for days (iron_god_pipeline_trace.gather enumerates every file), plus an unreproduced reading of the code. A directory listing is not the engine's current state.
entries.fix: Prove a claim is about CURRENT state before reporting it: run the engine's own function over live files filtered by regeneration time or identity, label anything else UNVERIFIED, and correct a wrong claim in the same channel immediately. An independent reviewer refused to implement a speculative scheduler change on the unverified lead.
entries.verification: Both claims were retracted with evidence in mailbox seq 175; the reviewer's agreement is mailbox seq 177 and 178. Request-file ages were measured (4443 minutes stale for the blamed request) and the engine functions were rerun on current requests only.
entries.regression_protection: ChatGPT recommended a regression fixture with stale and fresh requests and a separate pull request filtering the pipeline trace by authoritative current request identity (mailbox seq 178). Orchestrator pull request 689 is that change, OPEN and not merged at the time of recording: it filters by the head the refill recorded, keeps every in-flight request visible, and has tests for stale, fresh, old-file-current-head, in-flight and missing-head cases.
entries.residual_risk: Until pull request 689 merges and a release is promoted, iron_god_pipeline_trace still counts stale request files as current DECOMPOSITION_NOT_STARTED and the dashboard overstates stuck work. Even after it, a request still at the current head stays listed when the latest pass stopped deriving it (visible by design, not hidden).

entries.symptom: knowledge-engine-web roadmap-progress pull requests failed the types preflight check for days although the repository's own CI passed.
entries.root_cause: repository_environment() installed poetry.lock pins with pip install -r, and pip treats an installed git dependency with the same name and version as already satisfied, so a moved commit pin was ignored: the engine environment kept knowledge-engine-ai at 2eee4cc while the repository pins 746dfd5, and mypy could not find modules added later.
entries.fix: After the ordinary install, every name @ git+https pin is installed with --no-deps --force-reinstall, and the environment recipe version is bumped so existing environments rebuild once.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED, not RELEASE_DEPLOYED and not PRODUCT_VERIFIED. The cause was REPRODUCED by running mypy with the engine environment's own Python on main (5 errors), reading the installed direct_url.json commit, and a pip dry run; PR 685 merged with 193 passing tests in the lane test file and ruff clean. The knowledge-engine-web types check has not been rerun green on a promoted release.
entries.regression_protection: Tests: git_pin_reinstall_argv only touches git pins; a rebuilt environment runs both installs; a failing reinstall leaves the marker stale and is reported (follow-up test pull request).
entries.residual_risk: Not deployed: it takes effect only after the owner stages and promotes a release, so the running engine still has the defect. Non-https git sources are not produced by poetry_lock_pins and are not handled. Installed-versus-locked commit drift is still not observable in diagnostics.

entries.symptom: A failed roadmap-progress preflight recorded only the last 1500 characters of output, so the check that actually failed could not be read from the job result (KE-web types, VoiceStudio 37 backend test failures).
entries.root_cause: The runner stored output_tail[-1500:]; for a long run the tail is the summary line.
entries.fix: evidence_of() keeps short output whole and, for long output, the text from the first failure marker plus the last third of the budget, both verbatim with an omitted-characters marker.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED, not RELEASE_DEPLOYED. PR 684 merged; five new tests cover first failure kept with summary tail, short output whole, no-marker keeps tail, the result file uses the digest, and uppercase FAILED markers.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_iron_god_progress_preflight.py.
entries.residual_risk: Not deployed until a release is promoted. The preflight JSON report itself carries only per-check status, so a failing check's own output is still not captured when the report omits it.

entries.source_ref: mailbox seq 198 (contributed by ChatGPT): rocksmith#756 review
entries.symptom: A documentation pull request for the private Rocksmith library plan was reviewed and CI-checked after it was drafted, and two independent gates then found problems: Codex flagged a stale docs/project-status.yaml that still called issue 693 completed, and CI rejected a literal pull-request reference in roadmap_issue_queue that scripts/check_automation_readiness.py forbids.
entries.root_cause: The continuity file and the readiness contract were not consulted before the pull request was declared ready; the readiness script scans disposition and action text for operational status and pull-request references.
entries.fix: The continuity file was corrected in the same pull request, the queue was rewritten as issue-level durable outcomes with the pull-request provenance moved to verified_repository_state, the six workflows were rerun green and the pull request merged on the exact verified head.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED for the documentation change (rocksmith#756 merged after six green workflows at the exact head, per the contributor's mailbox report).
entries.regression_protection: scripts/check_automation_readiness.py and its tests enforce the contract; the practice of running the repository's AGENTS.md readiness checks before claiming green is not automated.
entries.residual_risk: Contributed lesson, not independently rerun by the recorder: run the repository's AGENTS.md and automation-readiness checks and read the status cache in the same pull request before claiming green.

entries.source_ref: mailbox seq 198-199 (contributed by ChatGPT): rocksmith#758 review
entries.symptom: The first differential comparator passed a synthetic happy path while two P1 review findings showed it could pass a repeated riff shifted in time and ignore residual onset error.
entries.root_cause: The acceptance metrics were exercised only on benign synthetic inputs; common bass riffs repeat pitch, so nearest-neighbour pairing camouflaged a global shift, and the fitted clock hid cancelling per-note errors.
entries.fix: Replaced nearest-onset pairing with an order-preserving alignment, added jitter, mistimed-note fraction and a competing-alignment guard to the verdict, and added the reviewers' exact cases as adversarial mutation tests.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED (rocksmith 758 merged after an independent exact-head review; 22 comparator tests), not RELEASE_DEPLOYED and not PRODUCT_VERIFIED: it has never been run against a real reference.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_corpus_differential.py adversarial cases: repeated-pitch riff, riff shifted by a beat, a bar and a period, cancelling errors, a few mistimed notes, a late first note.
entries.residual_risk: A synthetic happy path is not sufficient for acceptance metrics; thresholds still need calibration on real references before any PRODUCT_VERIFIED claim.

entries.source_ref: mailbox seq 198 (contributed by ChatGPT): evidence-state vocabulary
entries.symptom: Reports during the stall collapsed different levels of certainty into one word such as fixed or verified, so merged code was read as a deployed fix and a pull request as proof of product behaviour.
entries.root_cause: There was no shared vocabulary separating what was seen, what was reproduced, what was merged, what is running, and what a person confirmed on the real product.
entries.fix: Adopt five evidence states and name them in every status report and every lesson: OBSERVED, REPRODUCED, CODE_MERGED, RELEASE_DEPLOYED, PRODUCT_VERIFIED. Do not collapse them; a merge is not a deployment and a deployment is not product verification. In this store evidence_state VERIFIED means only that the lesson's own evidence was validated; it never means the fix is RELEASE_DEPLOYED or PRODUCT_VERIFIED, so read the verification and residual_risk text for the real state.
entries.verification: Applied in this learning-memory entry set: each fix lesson states its evidence state and what is not yet true (for example orchestrator 685 is CODE_MERGED, not RELEASE_DEPLOYED).
entries.regression_protection: Review of status reports against the vocabulary; no automated check.
entries.residual_risk: Not enforced by code; reports can still use the words loosely.

entries.source_ref: mailbox seq 198 (contributed by ChatGPT): coordination practice
entries.symptom: Mailbox receipts and acknowledgements were at risk of being read as proof that work was done, and the unacknowledged backlog (50 messages to one agent, 11 to the engine) mixed stale and live items.
entries.root_cause: The advisory mailbox records messages, not outcomes; GitHub is the authoritative record of work.
entries.fix: At the start and end of each session check the mailbox, reply and acknowledge only messages that were actually handled, track every action in GitHub, never treat a receipt as completion, and triage the backlog by newest and open work with no bulk acknowledgement.
entries.verification: Practised during this retrospective: the new messages were read, answered with GitHub references, and acknowledged individually.
entries.regression_protection: None automated.
entries.residual_risk: Historical snapshot, not a current count: on 2026-11-12 around 10:00 UTC the mailbox showed zero pending for ChatGPT, 67 for claude-code and 14 for the engine. Those old unacknowledged messages may be stale and have not been triaged.

entries.symptom: The local 7B planner named functions that do not exist in the module it was asked to edit (align_notes in alignment.py, twice), the plan was rejected, both attempts were spent and the slice returned to the capped capable builder.
entries.root_cause: The model was never shown the module's real function names; the outline prompt received only a file listing, and rejection feedback was truncated to 300 characters.
entries.fix: ground_edit_targets() snaps a target within 0.8 difflib similarity of exactly one real unit, otherwise reports the real unit names and the outline is asked once more with them; a made-up name that survives the retry is rejected as before. Code never guesses a target.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED (orchestrator 686; 105 decomposer tests; ruff clean), not RELEASE_DEPLOYED, with no fresh local rerun: the 7B planner has not been rerun on a promoted release, so it is not yet shown that the rejection no longer recurs. The hallucination was OBSERVED twice in the planner job records.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_iron_god_task_decomposer.py grounding tests (snap and trace, report with real names, left alone, a purpose naming another real unit blocks the snap, retry then pass, retry then still rejected).
entries.residual_risk: Not deployed until a release is promoted. A snap is a heuristic: it is traced and blocked when the purpose names a different real unit, but a close name can still be the wrong function. Costs at most one extra local model call.

entries.symptom: Delivered slices stayed PLANNED in engineering/capability-graph.json (Everward objective-cycle wiring, VoiceStudio s4-first-adapter), so the capable builder would redo finished work when its budget returned.
entries.root_cause: The engine records delivery through a roadmap-progress pull request, and that pull request is blocked when the repository's own preflight fails for unrelated reasons (VoiceStudio's 37 Windows-only test failures), so the graph never catches up.
entries.fix: Recorded the deliveries by hand in graph-record pull requests with verification text that states what is not shown, and reverted the Everward damage-repair slice to PLANNED after review because its test did not exercise the required paths.
entries.verification: Graph pull requests passed each repository's required checks; the engine's own parse_capability_graph and derive() were run on every edited graph to confirm the next executable slice.
entries.regression_protection: None automated.
entries.residual_risk: Any repository whose preflight baseline fails will keep delivered slices PLANNED; the progress step should record delivery independently of unrelated baseline failures.

entries.symptom: Two of my graph edits overstated or misdirected work: a slice was marked complete although its test used a setter rather than real impact handling and the Fix_It repair executor, and a new UI slice allowed frontend/** while the repository's only active UI is under electron/.
entries.root_cause: I compared the delivered work to the slice title instead of line by line to its acceptance criteria, and did not read the target repository's AGENTS.md before writing allowed paths.
entries.fix: Reverted the over-claim to PLANNED, pointed the slice at electron/** and added the repository's own UI rules to its acceptance; replied on the review threads and resolved them after the fix.
entries.verification: Both findings were fixed in the same pull requests before merge; the graphs still parse and derive.
entries.regression_protection: Review by Codex before merge caught both; the standing delegation requires resolving threads only after a proven fix.
entries.residual_risk: The practice (read AGENTS.md, compare acceptance line by line, write what is not shown into the verification text) is not enforced by code.

entries.symptom: Running pytest or the golden_song_v1 lane on a machine reported five false failures in tests/test_rocksmith_xml.py that CI did not have.
entries.root_cause: The installed rocksmith-cdlc-generator was an editable install of a different, older checkout, so plain pytest imported that copy instead of this checkout's src.
entries.fix: tests/test_checkout_import_path.py asserts the imported package lives under this checkout's src and says to use PYTHONPATH=src or reinstall.
entries.verification: Fails on the affected machine without PYTHONPATH and passes with it; with the checkout's own src the whole suite is 2221 passed, 3 skipped; CI passed on the pull request.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_checkout_import_path.py.
entries.residual_risk: Only the Rocksmith repository has the guard; other repositories can hit the same shadowing.

entries.symptom: I judged from the roadmap documents that knowledge-engine-ai had no remaining executable slice and that its automatic plan-next-work request would waste a capable-builder slot.
entries.root_cause: A documents-only audit read what the roadmap said was delivered; it did not read the tests. The builder read the tests and found that every online-evidence test builds its own hand-authored bundle, so none of them parse knowledge-engine-core's committed golden bundle and a field-level drift between the two parsers would go undetected.
entries.fix: The builder's pull request 211 added one PLANNED slice (vendor core's golden bundle at a pinned commit and test the adapter and report projection against it), marked nothing complete, and stated what its sandbox could not run.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED for the planning change only (knowledge-engine-ai 211); the slice itself is PLANNED and unimplemented. The merged pull request body, the added slice and its acceptance criteria were reviewed after the merge and no problem was found.
entries.regression_protection: None: the practice (read the tests as well as the docs before declaring no gap) is not automated.
entries.residual_risk: The slice is not implemented, so the drift risk still exists; the engine merged the pull request before an independent review, so review happened after the fact.

entries.symptom: The first version of the pipeline-trace fix hid requests that were still being worked: after an unrelated merge moved a repository's head, a request in flight kept its old exact_head and was classified as history.
entries.root_cause: The refill does not re-derive a request that is already open (a capable dispatch, a running planning or drafting job, a plan holding the parent), so such a request file keeps the head it was written at while it is live. A head comparison alone cannot tell history from live work.
entries.fix: gather() keeps every in-flight request visible: a capable dispatch with status DISPATCHED, a decomposer or drafter job in PLANNING, DRAFTING or VERIFYING, and a parent held by an ACTIVE plan. Finished dispatches and DONE plans with an old head are still history. A request still at the current head stays listed even if the latest pass stopped deriving it (visible by design).
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED (orchestrator 689, merged by the owner), not RELEASE_DEPLOYED. Checked read-only on the live engine state: 57 of 64 request files were history and the dispatched Everward, Rocksmith, VoiceStudio and knowledge-engine requests showed as current; a request 21 hours old was correctly kept, which a file-age rule would have hidden.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_iron_god_pipeline_trace.py: stale versus fresh, old file with current head, in-flight dispatch, running job and active plan, missing head, same-head leftover.
entries.residual_risk: Not deployed until a release is promoted. The same-head leftover case stays listed, so the dashboard can still overstate by a little. Diagnostics only: it changes what is reported, not what is built.

entries.source_ref: project-orchestrator#690 (Codex P2, ChatGPT mailbox seq 232 and 236)
entries.symptom: A planning guard meant to stop the 7B inventing a pure function that reads a file (analyze_guide_vocal on path/to/guide_vocal.wav, failed twice by the worker) also rejected legitimate pure filename parsers such as extension('song.wav').
entries.root_cause: The first rule treated any quoted media filename in an example as file access. A filename on its own is not file access; the failing plan had a path-like parameter, a path/to/ placeholder and structured data expected.
entries.fix: The guard now needs file-access evidence: a Path or stream annotation, a path/to/ placeholder, or a media, archive, model or database file literal passed to a path-like parameter with structured data (dict, list, tuple, set) expected. A filename parser (scalar answer, or a filename parameter) is accepted. The real failed plan is still rejected.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED (orchestrator 690, merged by the owner), not RELEASE_DEPLOYED. Verified against the engine's own handback diagnostics of the real failed plan, 112 decomposer tests, and regression tests for the false positive that two independent reviewers found before merge.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_iron_god_task_decomposer.py: media-file example rejected, Path annotation rejected, pure filename parser accepted, path-named parameter with a scalar answer accepted, the real failed plan still rejected.
entries.residual_risk: Dynamic I/O that matches none of the evidence patterns is still left to the worker's own attempt bounds. Not deployed until a release is promoted.

entries.source_ref: project-orchestrator#691 (Codex P2 x2, ChatGPT mailbox seq 245)
entries.symptom: With the capable builder's budget spent, the engine reported NO_READY_EXECUTION_SLICE although small locally buildable slices existed: the local builder was offered nothing from a repository whose head-of-line slice only the capable builder could take (observed 2026-11-12 on Rocksmith).
entries.root_cause: The compiler yields work for one capability per repository at a time, in roadmap order, and the graph contract forbids dropping an unfinished capability from the roadmap. The shortage was structural as well as a budget limit.
entries.fix: local_lookahead() asks the compiler again with the capabilities already offered moved behind the rest of the roadmap (reordered in memory, none dropped), keeps only requests that route LOCAL, looks at most four capabilities down, never offers a capability with unfinished dependencies, runs only when nothing on the head of the line routes LOCAL, and leaves the old behaviour if it fails. Review found two more gaps, both fixed with tests: a head capability already open with the capable builder is reported under skipped and must be set aside too, and the slice validator must fail on authority errors (SLICE_AUTHORITY_INCOMPLETE, CAPABILITY_GRAPH_INVALID, ALLOWED_PATHS_MISSING) instead of printing PASS. A validator script and docs/LOCAL_WORK_BACKLOG.md give authors the contract.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED (orchestrator 691), not RELEASE_DEPLOYED and not PRODUCT_VERIFIED. Real-repository probe in a throwaway lane with the live measured profile: the Rocksmith repair slice stayed with the capable builder and a local-sized slice behind it was offered to the local builder. 225 tests across the affected files at the first push, 124 after the fixes.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_iron_god_roadmap_refill.py lookahead tests (head capable and local behind, no lookahead when the head is local, depth bound, dependencies respected, pending head capability, pending middle capability, failure leaves behaviour unchanged) and tests/test_iron_god_validate_local_slice.py.
entries.residual_risk: No local build has run on a lookahead slice yet, so it is not shown that the 7B produces working code from these slices. A reviewer raised an unproven gap: a head that routes LOCAL but cannot run downstream suppresses the lookahead; it is judged bounded and transient but has not been reproduced. Not deployed until the owner promotes a release.

entries.symptom: Orchestrator 691 was merged at 21:46 UTC with an independent review already posted at 21:26 UTC that I had not read: it contained two actionable findings (a possible starvation gap and an ambiguity in a Rocksmith slice I wrote).
entries.root_cause: I treated the review request as pending and merged on the owner's instruction to build the update; the mailbox was not checked immediately before the merge, and the reviewer's status messages (WAITING_FOR_REVIEW) were the only ones I had seen.
entries.fix: The findings were read straight after the merge and acted on: the Rocksmith slice was corrected before the builder started it (rocksmith 763) and the lookahead gap was handed over for reproduction. Practice recorded: read the mailbox for the requested review immediately before merging a pull request a reviewer was asked to look at, and say in the merge message if a review is still outstanding.
entries.verification: Evidence state OBSERVED and corrected. Neither finding was a regression in merged behaviour: one concerned an unbuilt slice, the other an unproven gap.
entries.regression_protection: None automated.
entries.residual_risk: The same ordering mistake can recur; nothing checks the mailbox at merge time.

entries.symptom: A locally buildable slice I authored for section agreement said each generated section may satisfy at most one reference section, which allows first-come greedy pairing; the reviewer's counter-example scores 0.5 greedily but 1.0 with a maximum matching.
entries.root_cause: A prose rule such as at most one-to-one does not fix an algorithm, and the 7B follows the literal examples, so an under-specified rule plus examples that do not separate the algorithms would have been built wrong and accepted.
entries.fix: The slice now states the exact two-pointer algorithm that is maximum for start times on a line, defines a negative tolerance as zero, and pins the counter-example. An independent script implementing the stated algorithm was run against every example before committing and reproduced all seven answers.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED for the planning change only (rocksmith 763); the slice itself is PLANNED and unbuilt.
entries.regression_protection: Practice: for a locally built slice, name the algorithm when the choice matters and check the examples with an independent implementation. The slice validator checks example shape, not example correctness.
entries.residual_risk: The independent check was run by hand and is not part of the validator; a wrong example would still pass the validator.

entries.symptom: During the release preflight for 61d46f0, with the owner holding control and the engine stopped, an unrequested draft pull request appeared on rocksmith-cdlc-generator from a cloud run whose payload named a test fixture (cap-extra/extra-helper, add_two).
entries.root_cause: A product-lane test publishes a fixture graph with no measured local profile, so its slice routes CAPABLE, and the lane called the capable dispatch with the real process environment and the real network opener. The owner's laptop holds the real routine token, so the test fired a real, paid routine. The test lane is temporary, so the run was outside the six-per-day ledger. CI has no tokens and was never affected.
entries.fix: tests/conftest.py removes every CLAUDE_ROUTINE_ variable for every test, so the dispatch fails closed as CAPABLE_BUILDER_UNCONFIGURED; tests that need a token set a fake one. The unrequested pull request was closed unmerged at the owner's decision so the local builder could attempt the slice.
entries.verification: Evidence state CODE_MERGED (orchestrator 694). Mechanism read from the cloud run's own description, the fixture in tests/test_iron_god_product_lane.py and the lane's dispatch call. Two regression tests fail without the fixture change when a token is present.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_no_live_routine_tokens.py.
entries.residual_risk: Earlier preflights on the laptop were not audited for the same spend. The default opener is still the real network call: the credential is removed, the network is not blocked. Practice: a test suite that runs on a machine holding live credentials must strip them centrally, not rely on each test.

entries.symptom: The first local build reached through the lookahead (corpus-metric-arrangement-presence, release 61d46f0) failed 3 of 5 roadmap examples: the symmetric flag was wrong, and one repair turn did not fix it. Nothing merged.
entries.root_cause: The local drafter passed only the first 160 characters of the slice objective to the builder. The slice author (Claude) had opened the objective with background, so the rule (symmetric is true only when all three are present) was cut off and the 7B guessed. The slice validator passed and the examples had been checked by an independent script, but neither check looked at what the builder would actually be shown. The 7B had five correct examples and still wrote the wrong rule.
entries.fix: Planning: the two affected Rocksmith objectives now state the rule first (rocksmith 765). Engine: the roadmap objective gets the worker's whole 600-character bound, the planner's restatement is kept only when it fits whole, and the validator refuses a Level 1 objective longer than the builder is shown (orchestrator 695). The same change rejects a plan whose every example expects None, measured the same night on knowledge-engine-ai (copy_vendored_fixture).
entries.verification: Evidence state OBSERVED for the failure (engine request, draft result and handback read directly). The fixes are in review, not merged or deployed when this lesson was written. It is NOT shown that the 7B builds the slice correctly once it sees the rule.
entries.regression_protection: tests/test_iron_god_local_drafter.py (the real failed objective reaches the builder with its rule), tests/test_iron_god_validate_local_slice.py (length limit), tests/test_iron_god_task_decomposer.py (effect-only plan).
entries.residual_risk: Practice for slice authors: rule in the first sentence, background last; before committing a local slice, look at the text the builder will receive, not only at the validator result. Correct examples do not rescue a missing rule. A rule in words is necessary; whether it is sufficient for the 7B is unmeasured.
